sections.h2: What does the Henry County Clerk of Superior Court do for a home sale?
sections.html:
The clerk's Real Estate Division is where a Henry County deed becomes part of the public record. The county's court pages list its work under Deeds and Liens, Fees, Locating Records, Notary Public, Plats, Trade Names, Uniform Commercial Code filings, Miscellaneous Information and the Filing Activity Notification System, known as FANS. A sale is not complete on the public record until the deed is filed here with the transfer tax paid.

The same office has divisions you may also meet during a sale or a dispute: Civil, Criminal, Finance, Jury, Passport Services and an Administrative Division that houses the Board of Equalization. The clerk's page also carries an I Want To list with an entry for appealing your property taxes, and it points to a cost schedule for civil and criminal filings.

  • Search records: the Locating Records page covers searching deeds, liens and property records online.
  • Electronic filing: the court site has an eFile Real Estate Records page that routes through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.
  • Fees: the Fees page under the Real Estate Division is the place to confirm current recording costs before you mail or e-file a deed.

sections.h2: What is the Georgia real estate transfer tax, and who pays it in Henry County?
sections.html:
The transfer tax is an excise tax on a sale, separate from the annual property tax. Georgia's clerks' authority states that it must be paid before the clerk will record a deed, and that the clerk then attaches a certification that it has been paid. The seller pays it unless the contract says otherwise.

The rate printed in the state's filing help is $1 for the first $1,000, or fraction of $100 to $1,000, and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100. The form itself shows the line as tax due at .10 per $100, with a $1.00 minimum. Henry County follows that statewide rate because the tax is set by the state, not the county.

PT-61 filing rules as stated by the Georgia clerks' authority

Warranty or other transfer deedYes, even if no money changes hands

Most leases, except an estate for yearsNo

sections.h2: How do I complete the PT-61 for a Henry County deed?
sections.html:
You complete it online through the clerks' authority website, which does not charge for the form and needs no account. After you submit, print the confirmation copy, bring it to the closing, and file it with the deed package at the clerk's office if the closing succeeds. Only one PT-61 goes with each deed. No signature is required, but the filer must check a box confirming the information is true and correct to the best of their knowledge.

  • Enter the county, and the city when the house sits inside city limits.
  • Enter a map and parcel number. If none was assigned, the form accepts N/A.
  • List the previous owner as the seller, not a real estate agent or auction company.
  • If you spot an error after filing, tell the clerk's office. Before filing, submit a fresh form and discard the bad one.

The help desk phone is 800-304-5174. A property that crosses a county line needs a deed and a PT-61 in each county, with the price pro-rated between them and an affidavit describing the split. Exemptions from paying the tax are built into the online form, and the form shows the legal basis for each one you select.

sections.h2: What do Henry County property taxes have to do with recording?
sections.html:
Property tax is separate from the recording step, but a sale touches both. Henry County's Tax Commissioner bills the January 1 owner and files a lien against that owner unless a settlement statement arrives within 90 days of the due date, citing Georgia Code 48-3-3. The statement goes by email to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov. The commissioner's bill page prints November 16 as the due date and says bills go out by mid-September.

A second tax applies to loans. The Georgia Department of Revenue says anyone holding a long-term note secured by real estate must record the security instrument in the county where the land sits within 90 days. The intangible recording tax is $1.50 for each $500 or fractional part of the note's face amount. In most counties the clerk collects it, and in others the tax commissioner does, so ask which office takes it in Henry County before a refinance or a buyer's mortgage closes.

  • Transfer tax: usually the seller's cost, collected at recording.
  • Intangible recording tax: tied to the lender's security instrument, not to a cash purchase.
  • Property tax: billed to the January 1 owner, with a county lien if unpaid.

sections.h2: What does Henry County look like for sellers who record deeds here?
sections.html:
Henry County had about 264,922 residents in the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate and 97,759 housing units. It covers 318.71 square miles of land, so recording volume is substantial for a county of its size. The county issued 1,666 building permits in 2025, which means new-build deeds and plats arrive alongside resales.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024: $313,900.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 74.9%.
  • Households: 86,704.
  • Median gross rent: $1,674.

The county sits about 25 miles southeast of Atlanta and includes McDonough, Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove, according to its financial report. A deed for a house in any of the four cities is recorded at the same Henry County clerk, since the clerk's office works at the county level and not the city level.

sections.h2: What should I check before my deed is filed?
sections.html:
Get the legal description, the map and parcel number and the names exactly as they appear on the prior deed. Missing parcel data is one of the few things the state form insists on. Confirm the transfer tax amount and who is paying it with the closing agent, since the contract can shift the tax away from the seller.

  • Ask whether your closing agent will e-file through the clerks' authority or deliver paper to the clerk.
  • Confirm that any security deed being paid off has a release ready to record.
  • Request the plat if the lot was recently divided. Henry's clerk keeps a Plats page for copies.
  • Check the Henry County Tax Commissioner for an open lien or unpaid current bill.

Once the deed is recorded, the deed book and page number is cross-referenced to the PT-61 reference number, and the PT-61 data travels to the Department of Revenue and the tax assessors so the ownership record on the tax rolls updates.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Henry County, Georgia?
faqs.a: Record it with the Henry County Clerk of Superior Court, Real Estate Division. The clerk's court pages list Deeds and Liens, Fees, Locating Records and an eFile option for real estate records through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a Henry County sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays unless the sales contract says otherwise. The clerks' authority states the tax is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction. It must be paid before the clerk records the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a PT-61 form to remove a name from a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The clerks' authority says a PT-61 is required whenever ownership changes, even with no money exchanged, unless the document falls into one of four exempt categories. Some changes are also exempt from the tax itself.

faqs.q: Is a PT-61 needed for a transfer on death deed?
faqs.a: Not at the time of recording, since no property is conveyed yet. After the owner dies and the beneficiary files an affidavit accepting the real estate, a PT-61 is required.

faqs.q: How do I search for a recorded deed in Henry County?
faqs.a: Use the Locating Records page under the clerk's Real Estate Division, which describes online searching of deeds, liens and property records. Call the Clerk of Superior Court if you cannot find an older instrument.
